items.title: Trillium Health Partners launches $1B campaign for massive new Mississauga hospital
items.summary: The future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital will replace the existing Mississauga Hospital and will house the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children. A rendering of the Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital. This summary was produced using artificial intelligence and reviewed by an editor for accuracy and clarity. Trillium Health Partners Foundation has launched a $1-billion fundraising campaign to build Canada’s largest hospital in Mississauga. The future Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital will replace the existing Mississauga Hospital. It will house the Shah Family Hospital for Women and Children, touted as the province’s first hospital dedicated to women’s and children’s health. According to the hospital foundation, the newly launched Built for Us campaign expands on investments from the province and the City of Mississauga alongside “transformational support” from private donors. “To date we’ve raised about $600 million,” said Caroline Riseboro, foundation president and CEO, in an interview. The foundation aims to raise the remaining $400 million by 2032. The Peter Gilgan Mississauga Hospital is expected to open in late 2033 or early 2034, Riseboro said.

items.title: ‘Radio silent’: Fans still waiting on refunds a month after comedy festival in Mississauga was postponed
items.summary: Brenna Oude-Reimerink just wants her money back. A month after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival was abruptly postponed, she says she hasn’t heard a word from organizers about the $394 she spent on two VIP tickets. The festival was scheduled to happen at Erindale Park, near the University of Toronto Mississauga, from Sept. 11 to 13. Several big names in comedy were billed for the weekend, including Stavros Halkias, John Mulaney and Jeff Arcuri, who Oude-Reimerink was most excited to see. Oude-Reimerink sprung for two VIP tickets for Sept. 12, paying roughly $394 for the seats, and purchasing the pair through the third-party ticket supplier used by the festival. The VIP tickets promised exclusive entry lanes, and table service during the event. “My sister and I were really looking forward to seeing him live. We’ve never seen him before,” Oude-Reimerink said in an interview with CTV News Toronto. The comedy festival sent out an email on the morning of Sept. 7, reviewed by CTV News Toronto, detailing everything to know ahead of the festival from when doors opened to where to park and what could be brought into the grounds. A day later, festival organizers announced they would be postponing the festival without providing a clear reason why. “We know there was a lot of excitement around the show, but our priority is to deliver the best possible festival, and we believe that postponing this week’s performance is the right decision to ensure we can do that,” the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival wrote in a statement posted online Sept.

items.title: A clash of titans or old guard versus new? Inside the epic battle for Mississauga
items.summary: Why this might be the closest race Mississauga has seen in a very long time. From left, incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish, former Mayor Bonnie Crombie and former councillor Alvin Tedjo, who are in an epic battle for the mayoralty in Mississauga. In the run-up to this month’s municipal election, the Star is profiling several key battleground races, offering intimate portraits of the candidates and the issues moving voters. In today’s spotlight is Mississauga. The Mississauga mayoral race has been a winding Shakespearean tale featuring a 15-year rivalry, a possibly hubristic return, a debate stage duel, the sudden emergence of a dark horse and the looming presence of a ghost. There is incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who realized her decades-old dream of becoming mayor when then-mayor Bonnie Crombie quit to become Ontario Liberal leader. There is Crombie, who succeeded the inimitable Hazel McCallion after her 36-year tenure, won her third mayoral election in a landslide and is invoking McCallion’s name to do so again in a high-stakes comeback following her failed bid to oust Premier Doug Ford. And, inching closer in the nailbitingly tight polls, is Alvin Tedjo, a rookie councillor who grew up in downtown Mississauga where his Chinese-Indonesian parents settled when he was four. Tedjo started the race polling behind his council colleague Dipika Damerla, but now seems to have swept past her and into the role of the generational change candidate. “I think it’s very fluid,” said Councillor Brad Butt (a Parrish supporter) of the race.

items.title: Who is Dipika Damerla? Secunderabad roots, Bollywood twist to her Mississauga mayoral bid
items.summary: HYDERABAD: From childhood visits to her grandparents in Secunderabad to a career in Canadian politics, Telugu-origin Dipika Damerla’s journey has taken her from Hyderabad’s cantonment area to the mayoral race in Mississauga, Ontario, as reported by TOI. A former provincial minister and an eight-year city councillor, Damerla is campaigning on better civic services, affordability and economic growth. She is using an unconventional mix of policy promises and Bollywood songs to reach voters ahead of the October 26 municipal election. Mississauga’s municipal election will choose the mayor, ward and regional councillors, and school board trustees for the 2026–2030 term. Damerla, who represents Ward 7 on the city council, is seeking to move from local representation to the city’s top elected office. Born in Secunderabad into a family with an Army background, Damerla moved frequently because of her father’s postings. Her grandparents’ home, however, kept her connected to the city. She recalls visits to Monda Market and Secunderabad Club. She studied at Raja Jitendra Public School in Begumpet and Kendriya Vidyalaya in Trimulgherry before moving to Canada in 1991 after her marriage. “We had Satyanarayan kathas and relatives visiting our house often. The Telugu films screened at Sheesh Mahal are an integral part of my memories. Those four years in Hyderabad were unforgettable,” she told to the Media in a brief interview from Canada. Her campaign has recently drawn attention for its use of Bollywood music. On October 9, following a mayoral debate, Damerla posted a video on X reworking the song ‘Kya Hua Tera Wada’.

This makes Mississauga 173rd out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. As of July 1, 2026 in Ontario, some previously mandatory accident benefits are now optional. ca data, drivers in Mississauga pay about $3,078 per year for auto insurance as of March 2026. Drivers here pay premiums that are higher than in Burlington, which is the cheapest city for car insurance in the GTA at $2,109 per year. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. 2% higher. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. The lowest average premium in Mississauga is found in the L5K area, where drivers pay $2,737 annually. Meanwhile, drivers in L4T have the highest average premiums at $3,937 per year.

items.title: Peel Region's South Asian Film Festival Marks 15 Years With a Shift Toward Local Talent
items.summary: According to CBC, the International Film Festival of South Asia is celebrating its 15th year as a Peel Region cultural institution. The outlet reports the anniversary marks a turning point for the festival, which started out curating films from around the world and is now building an ecosystem meant to help local South Asian filmmakers get their work made and seen. CBC Peel's Nav Nanwa hosted this year's gala on Friday in Brampton, a city that sits alongside Mississauga in the heart of the GTA's South Asian community. Nanwa spoke with organizers and attendees before taking the stage, gathering their reflections on how far the festival has come. CBC says the milestone event highlights the growing presence of homegrown South Asian filmmaking talent across the region.

items.title: Mississauga Mayoral Candidate Channels Bollywood to Promise No Property Tax Hike
items.summary: According to the Deccan Chronicle, Mississauga mayoral candidate Dipika Damerla is drawing attention in Ontario's municipal election with a campaign video built around a reworked Bollywood song. The outlet reports Damerla, born in Secunderabad, completed her MBA in Toronto before winning election to Mississauga city council in 2018. She went on to serve seven years as the Ontario Liberal MPP for Mississauga East-Cooksville, including time as associate minister for long-term care and later as minister responsible for seniors affairs. The Deccan Chronicle says Damerla worked in corporate banking and ran her own business in Mississauga before entering politics. In the video shared on X, she sings a modified version of the Bollywood song 'Kya Hua Tera Wada' and pledges that property taxes will not rise if she becomes mayor. The outlet reports the video closes with her campaign slogan, 'A city that works,' alongside an appeal for voter support. The City of Mississauga's own website confirms Damerla served as the Ward 7 councillor beginning in 2018.

items.title: Here's What ID Voters Need to Bring to Advance Polls in Ontario's Municipal Election
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, advance polls have opened in parts of Ontario ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election, and voters need to bring proper identification to cast a ballot. The outlet reports a Canadian passport does not count as valid ID for voting purposes, since voters write their own address inside it rather than having it printed by the issuing authority. Mississauga.com says residents who are currently unhoused, or whose identification has been lost or stolen, still have options available to them to vote without standard ID. The outlet is encouraging voters to confirm exactly when and where advance polls are open in their own community ahead of election day. Mississauga.com reports the identification rules apply across the province as municipalities prepare for the Oct. 26 vote.

items.title: Remembering the life of ERMA McPHERSON CRUMP
items.summary: McPHERSON CRUMP, ERMA GRACE (nee BRANKLEY) Passed away at Markham Stouffville Hospital on September 6, 2026. Beloved wife of the late Paul McPherson, and loving mother of Cheryl, Scott (Susan) and Craig (Natalina). Proud grandmother of Christian, Rachel, Matthew and Olivia. Erma also found love a second time with the late Donald Crump and adored her extended family of Susan (the late Tom Kral), Nancy (Jason Kea) and grandchildren, Erin, Damon, Julia and Alison. Dear sister of Roy (Maureen) and Arlene. Erma was an active golfer and curler at Bayview Golf & Country Club for over 20 years and made long-lasting friendships there. She also made numerous new friends in the Ballantrae community, played bridge and joined a book club. Erma loved to travel, taking in the history of the many countries that she visited. Erma knew the importance of family and friends and cherished those moments spent together. m. In lieu of flowers, please consider a donation to your favourite charity in Erma's name. items.title: Mississauga Council Creates Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force to Guide Future Planning Rules
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city council unanimously approved a motion from Coun. Sue McFadden on Sept. 29 to create a temporary task force focused on shaping planning rules around large-scale data centres. The outlet reports the task force will include council members, municipal planning staff, industry representatives and local residents, and is meant to operate on a short-term basis. McFadden told council it was important to bring in residents from wards 9 and 10, where applications for hyperscale data centres have been most active. Mississauga.com says the task force decision comes two weeks after council approved a temporary two-year freeze, through an interim control bylaw passed Sept. 16, on new and existing data centre applications across the city. The outlet reports the task force is meant to help guide the city's broader planning review while that freeze stays in effect.
